subject: wolves
one_liner: A photo network for wolves where reach is measured in kilometers of audible howl and the feed is ranked by rank.
brand_voice_notes: Deadpan network-infrastructure register. Range never calls itself social. It calls itself distribution. Wolves are 'nodes', packs are 'relay partners', howling is 'acoustic handoff', and hierarchy is not a bug the company is working on, it is the ranking model and they are proud of it. Copy is written like a status page maintained by people who have accepted four-night delivery latency as a physical constant. Never warm, never winking. The only emotion permitted anywhere on the page belongs to the omega in the second testimonial, and the company does not appear to notice it.

hero.h1: Every wolf is a distribution channel.
hero.sub: Range is the photo network for pack animals. Post a kill, mark the range it came from, and let the howl relay carry it across nine adjacent territories before the ravens file their version.

features.title: Howl Relay
features.blurb: Posts propagate by acoustic handoff. One howl moves your photograph roughly 11 km, then holds until a neighboring pack repeats it. Median delivery is four nights. Weather adds two. We have modeled this extensively and consider it acceptable.

features.title: Hierarchy Feed
features.blurb: The feed is ranked by rank. Breeding pairs surface first in every territory they border, permanently. Mid-pack wolves may purchase placement by the night. Omegas are shown their own posts, which our retention data suggests is sufficient.

features.title: Scent-Verified Posting
features.blurb: Every upload is authenticated against a marked perimeter before it enters the relay. If the scent does not match the geotag, the post is held for review by an unaffiliated pack with no standing in the dispute. Appeals resolve within one season.

pricing_tiers.name: Omega
pricing_tiers.tagline: Post freely. Nothing leaves the den.
perks: A feed consisting entirely of your own posts, in order
One howl per lunar cycle, unamplified
Scent verification on a single marker, renewed annually

pricing_tiers.name: Territorial
pricing_tiers.tagline: For wolves with a perimeter to defend.

Relay priority through two adjacent packs
Denning-season archive with automatic litter tagging

pricing_tiers.name: Apex

testimonials.quote: I posted an elk femur at moonrise. By the third night it had reached the Sawtooth pack. By the fifth it had reached a pack I have never met and would kill on sight. That is reach.
testimonials.name: Grey Marla
testimonials.title: Breeding Female, Lower Bitterroot Pack

testimonials.quote: The hierarchy feed showed me my own posts for eleven months. I assumed the network was small. I have since been told there are four thousand wolves on it.
testimonials.name: Tuck
testimonials.title: Omega, Nine Mile Pack (transfer pending)

testimonials.quote: Our relay contract stipulates six wolves howling in sequence at 0340. Two of them are not committed to the work and you can see it in the kilometer numbers.
testimonials.name: Anders Rulle
testimonials.title: Head of Acoustic Distribution, Northern Range Operations

demo_screen_concept: The Range feed console: a dark bento lattice of wolf posts (a ridgeline at moonrise, a three-quarter face portrait, a wolf mid-howl, two wolves nose to nose in snow), each tile carrying a rank badge (ALPHA / MID-PACK / OMEGA), a scent-verification state (VERIFIED, PENDING, HELD), and a howl-relay meter showing kilometers traveled and how many adjacent packs have repeated it. A live audible-range figure ticks in the header. Filter chips switch the feed between HIERARCHY (default, breeding pairs pinned to the top and not removable), NEAREST RANGE, and CHRONOLOGICAL (disabled, with a tooltip reading 'Territorial and above'). Clicking a tile opens a detail sheet listing the full relay chain by pack name, timestamp, and distance, plus a HOWL button that appends your pack to the chain and animates the kilometer figure upward by one hop.

images.rationale: Whole budget on demo subject assets, because on a photo network the posts are the product. Hero image skipped: the direction is a monochrome typographic bento and the hero earns more from a live feed plate built out of the same post tiles than from a decorative wolf. Testimonial headshots skipped: all three quotes keep matching CSS monogram plates with pack IDs, which stays consistent and lets the bone/basalt lattice carry the section. Four 1:1 near-monochrome wolf photographs fill the demo feed grid and the two hero feed tiles.

design_direction.style: Quarantined-accent monochrome bento lattice, basalt dark mode. The page is staged as the product site of a heavily funded photo network that has decided the wolf is a distribution channel and files pack hierarchy under ranking model. A flat basalt near-black ground (#0B0C0B) runs the whole page with no gradients, no glow, no texture washes, and no glass: panels are flat surface fills one shade lighter (#141614) inside 1px hairline borders (#262A25) at a uniform 14px radius, and every shadow is banned, so depth comes only from the lattice, the hairlines, and two rationed colors. The organizing move is the bento lattice: a 12-column grid where every section resolves into modular tiles of varied span (a 7-col claim beside a 5-col feed plate, 4/4/4 feature tiles, a 8/4 telemetry split, three pricing tiles of unequal height), tiles butted at a constant 14px gutter so the page reads as a network console someone has laid out for a board deck. The core motif is the inversion tile: exactly one tile per section flips to a solid bone flood (#EFEBE1) with basalt type knocked out of it, marking whatever the ranking model has decided is alpha in that section, never explained. The second motif is the howl meter: a horizontal row of thin vertical bone bars of stepped height, built in CSS, that reads as an audio signature and doubles as the relay progress indicator, list bullet, and pricing tier gauge, with repeated packs filling in bone and unreached packs left at 12% opacity. Bone (#EFEBE1) is the sole carrier: the wordmark, every primary CTA, one word per headline, and the inversion tiles, all as flat floods with basalt knocked out. One rationed arterial red (#E64B38) is quarantined strictly to live pack telemetry (relay-active dots, kilometers currently in flight, HELD verification states, rival-sighting counts, the disabled chronological chip) and appears nowhere else on the page, so the only color on a monochrome site is always something the network is worried about. Syne sets the wordmark and headlines in wide-set geometric grotesque with infrastructure-company-that-raised-a-C confidence, tracking tightened to -0.02em at display sizes; IBM Plex Sans carries plain, faintly status-page body copy. Every figure that pretends to be network telemetry (kilometers relayed, hop counts, pack IDs, latency in nights, tier prices) is set in IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures inside inset basalt wells one shade darker than the tile, so it reads like the console, not marketing. Motion is lattice-restrained: tiles brighten their hairline to bone at 30% on hover with no lift and no scale change, howl meters fill left to right once on scroll, the arterial relay dot pulses on a 4s cycle, CTAs depress 1px on press, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No light mode, no glass, no blur panels, no clay shadow pairs, no offset sticker shadows, no hairline print rules or double-rule frames, no catalog stitching, no didone engraving, no storefront capsules, no nautical chrome, no engraved seals, no aurora washes, no mirrored type, no emoji. Reads like a company that files the pack bond under 'graph topology' and considers the raven a competing publisher.

fonts.body: 'IBM Plex Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

design_direction.archetype: Consumer social-network product page staged as distribution infrastructure: bento hero splitting a monumental typographic claim against a live feed plate, a relay telemetry strip, three feature tiles with one inverted, testimonial tiles with monogram plates and pack IDs, three pricing tiles as network tiers, closing CTA band, handoff to the feed console demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Hairline brightening on hover with no lift or scale, howl meters filling left to right once on scroll, a 4s arterial relay pulse, 1px CTA depression on press, 6px section fade-ups staggered 40ms, all behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: 12-column bento: a 7-column claim tile carrying the Syne headline with one bone-flooded word, the sub, and the primary CTA; a 5-column feed plate beside it showing two real post tiles with rank badges, scent state, and howl meters, stacked so the lattice reads as product not decoration. Below, a full-width 4-tile telemetry strip in IBM Plex Mono (kilometers relayed tonight, packs in chain, median latency in nights, ranges under verification) with the arterial relay dot live on exactly one figure. Mobile collapses to a single column, feed plate second, telemetry strip to a 2x2.
